notes.title: Title, composer and lyricist
notes.statement: Title and composer are present in the score properties and displayed. Title is at the top of the page, centred; composer is at the right-hand side, just below the title. For songs, the lyricist is at the left-hand side, just below the title, roughly in line with the composer.

notes.title: Dedication
notes.statement: Use a separate vertical frame above the main title frame, centred and italicised, at the templating stage.

notes.title: Dates are not shown
notes.statement: Birth and death dates are not shown for anyone (composer, lyricist or dedicatee). Some of that data is stored separately in the project data.

notes.title: Date of composition
notes.statement: The date of composition is not shown in the title frame. A date and place of composition may be shown at the end of the score if it appears in the source.

notes.title: Provenance is stored, not rendered
notes.statement: Provenance (source edition and file, pages, transcriber, reviewer, licence, tools, and the Principles, profile and Notes versions) is stored in the project data and not rendered by default. The editorial report repeats the source details.

notes.title: Entering source breaks
notes.statement: Follow the source's system breaks first and page breaks second. Enter them with the app's standard break elements (not spacers or manual position offsets) so that removal is a single operation. Never split a bar across a break.
details: Omit all breaks in extreme cases (very small pages, or music transcribed from parts) and say so in the report.

notes.title: Above and below the stave
notes.statement: Use the template defaults. Above the stave go tempo marks and playing instructions such as pizz. and arco. Below go all dynamics, hairpins and expression text.
exceptions: Quartets: where one voice is arco and another pizz., place each above or below as suits its voice.
All: with several expressive markings at once, it can help to flip some to the other side.
Lieder: dynamics in the vocal parts go above.

notes.title: Default beaming
notes.statement: Enter notes with the default beaming for the time signature. Editorial conventions for 6/8, for example, vary between editions, so they are normalised.

notes.title: Beam placement
notes.statement: Beams go all above or all below the noteheads, not a combination of both.
exceptions: String parts never use beams with noteheads on both sides. Lieder piano parts sometimes need it, for example when crossing between treble and bass of the grand stave.

notes.title: Telling composer-led grouping from house style
notes.statement: Copy a non-standard grouping when it appears to be the composer's own choice for a passage (Bartok is a classic case). If you cannot tell, keep the source grouping and record an observation (`read.composer-led-grouping`).
details: Signals of composer-led grouping: it departs from the norm only in that passage; it recurs identically when the material recurs; it plainly serves the music (regrouping the metre, showing a phrase); or other sources agree.
Signals of house style: the same habit applies across the whole edition regardless of the music.

notes.title: Beams across a system break
notes.statement: Do not copy a beam that would continue across a barline at a system break if the app has no provision for it. Separate the beam groups at that barline.

notes.title: Rest grouping
notes.statement: Use the time-signature defaults. This can diverge visibly from the source; that is fine if consistent. State it once in the report.

notes.title: Tuplet settings
notes.statement: Use the default bracket whatever the source uses. In the Inspector set Direction = Auto, Number type = Number and Bracket type = Auto.
details: In a long passage that is consistently in one tuplet, show the first marking and make the rest invisible. They stay in the file, so playback and export are unaffected.

notes.title: Tremolo
notes.statement: Prefer the app's default form of a measured tremolo.

notes.title: Tempo marks
notes.statement: Include tempo marks as in the source, with metronome marks, above the stave. Keep tempo terms in the source language, with a bracketed translation for non-standard ones (`text.translation-format`). Gradual changes (rit., accel.) are lines and follow `dynamics.terms` and `dynamics.ritardando-line`.

notes.title: Ornament placement
notes.statement: Use the defaults for exact placement (for example before or after the barline).

notes.title: Nearest available form
notes.statement: When a grace note group cannot be entered exactly, use the nearest form in the order the rule gives, and add staff text for a tuplet indication only if it is useful.

notes.title: No cancelling naturals
notes.statement: Never show cancelling naturals on a change of key signature. Never use the "Natural-flat" or "Natural-sharp" symbols for individual cancellation in adjacent measures.

notes.title: Added accidentals
notes.statement: Enclose any accidental you introduce (one not in the source) in square brackets [] and list each in the report.

notes.title: Decision order for viola and cello
notes.statement: (a) Keep the source clef where `clef.preserved-clefs` lists it. (b) Apply the leger-line test in `clef.leger-line-test` to brief changes. (c) Use `clef.other-clefs-modern` for any clef not listed.

notes.title: Two clefs by default
notes.statement: Most work is set in two clefs, treble and bass.

notes.title: Clefs to preserve
notes.statement: Preserve these clefs, subject to `clef.leger-line-test`. Lieder: treble clef with 8 beneath it (down an octave), typical for the tenor voice in modern editions (solo and choral). Viola: mostly alto clef, with occasional treble passages. 'Cello: bass, tenor and treble.
exceptions: Cello treble clef is notated at the sounding octave, per modern convention. Some sources (for example Dvorak and Beethoven) use a de facto treble clef an octave lower; we avoid that practice.

notes.title: Leger-line test for brief clef changes
notes.statement: Omit or adapt brief clef changes where a source seems to prioritise page space over readability. For viola and cello, change clef only if you would need more than 2 leger lines and the passage stays high long enough to help the player. Use the clef a modern player would expect, and report it.
details: Some transcribers use the original clefs while transcribing (see `workflow.original-clefs`). An algorithmic approach to modern clef choice exists in the [Species corpus](https://github.com/MarkGotham/species) and may be formalised later.

notes.title: Other clefs to modern equivalents
notes.statement: Adapt any clef not listed in `clef.preserved-clefs` (soprano, mezzo-soprano, baritone, French violin clef) to its nearest modern equivalent. The cello clefs in `clef.preserved-clefs` are preserved.

notes.title: No manual stem flips
notes.statement: Almost never flip a note's stem manually. This also matters for transposition and clef changes.

notes.title: Terms
notes.statement: Copy the source, except where an alternative is clearly equivalent and more standard today (for example diminuendo or dim. for decrescendo).

notes.title: Abbreviations
notes.statement: Use the recognised standards cresc., dim., rit., rall. and accel. Spell out anything even slightly ambiguous, or adapt it to one of these.

notes.title: Words spread over several bars
notes.statement: For cre - - - scen - - - do across bars or systems, use a wide-dashed line (Line Thickness = 0.12sp, Dash Line Length = 5, Dash Gap Width = 20) with standard Begin text and a Continue text in parentheses at the start of each system, for example (dim.).

notes.title: Ritardando line
notes.statement: Use the app's built-in ritardando line where it exists. Earlier scores used a System text entry instead; these may be updated. Record the app and version in the report header.

notes.title: Accidentals across ties
notes.statement: An accidental is not repeated at the start of the second (or later) bar of a tie, even at a system or page break. If the same pitch recurs later in that bar, the accidental is shown (a default, and worth keeping).

notes.title: Square brackets mark what we add
notes.statement: Square brackets in our files mark only what we add (accidentals, translations). Every other intervention is reported, not marked.

notes.title: Keep the source's brackets
notes.statement: In a direct transcription, keep the brackets (square or curved) that the source prints around a note, accidental or similar, as printed where the encoding expresses them, and otherwise record them in the report. They signal an intervention by the source's edition. Downstream editions may drop them (see `editorial.downstream-editions`).

notes.title: Telling the source's brackets from ours
notes.statement: Keep the source's brackets distinguishable from ours. Carry the distinction in the data where the format allows, and always in the report. Where the source also uses square brackets, the report lists which are ours.

notes.title: Standard palette entries
notes.statement: Where the app has a standard entry for a technique or similar instruction, use it with its standard (Italian) wording, whatever the source says. These are pizz. and arco (from the text palette; placement as in `layout.above-below`) and con sord. and senza sord. for mutes. The entries drive playback, part extraction and export. Almost no other terms have this status, so for everything else the source language stands.

notes.title: Harmonics
notes.statement: Include harmonics, from the articulations palette (the symbol looks like o).

notes.title: String indications
notes.statement: Include any instruction giving the string, for example sul A or IV.

notes.title: Fingerings are not transcribed
notes.statement: Fingering is classed as unsupported in our profile. The version-of-record format (KRN) has no fingering in its core vocabulary and the profile accepts no extension for it (`fmt.fingering`), so printed fingerings are not transcribed. State this once in each report.
exceptions: Where a fingering works as an implicit string instruction, include it.

notes.title: Translations
notes.statement: Give a translation of a non-standard term in square brackets after the term in the same text item, for example Sehr langsam [Very slowly]. If it would clutter the score, put it in the report instead.

notes.title: Red text while working
notes.statement: While transcribing, use red staff text to explain an intentional deviation from the source and to mark anything suspicious, including a correction you did not make. Before release, convert each red text into a report entry (`declare.report-deviations`) or an observation (`declare.observations`), then delete it. A release contains no red text.

notes.title: Handling a suspected source error
notes.statement: Transcribe it as printed, mark it with red text while working, and record an observation in the report (`declare.observations`, `editorial.observations`). If the error passes the clear-error test (`correct.error-test`), the observation names the one minimal change, so that a correction can be recorded (`correct.record`).

notes.title: Consistency edits
notes.statement: Make equivalent notations match, but do not edit a divergence that might be musical (an articulation that differs in one part, a different pitch in a recurring motive). Preserve it and record an observation (`declare.observations`). Harmonising is editorial.

notes.title: A case no rule or Note covers
notes.statement: Keep what the source prints and record an observation (`stance.doubt-means-preserve`, `declare.observations`). Topics listed under "Outside this version" have no Note yet and are handled this way.

notes.title: Manuscripts
notes.statement: Manuscripts and other special sources are out of scope for this profile (`unsupported_sources` in the profile) and are not transcribed under it.

notes.title: Original clefs while transcribing
notes.statement: Some transcribers use the original clefs while transcribing, to make proofreading easier (comparing a notehead on the same line or space). Before release the clefs follow `clef.preserved-clefs`, `clef.leger-line-test` and `clef.other-clefs-modern`.

notes.title: What is reported
notes.statement: Report any deviation from the source that is not visibly marked in the score. The report covers at least the following.
details: Added accidentals (also bracketed in the score).
Grouping kept as printed because composer-led and house-style grouping could not be told apart (as an observation).
Ornaments or details entered in the nearest available form.
Which brackets are ours, where the source also uses square brackets (`brackets.tell-apart`).

notes.title: Systematic and specific entries
notes.statement: State systematic differences once, in a general note that lists the normalisations applied. Give each specific intervention one row, with bar, part or staff, source reading, our reading, reason and rule ID.

examples.situation: A clef is changed in a cello part.
examples.handling: b. 34, Vc.: clef changed to tenor; passage stays above the stave for 9 bars (`clef.leger-line-test`).

notes.title: Report header
notes.statement: Source edition and file, pages, transcriber, reviewer, date, the app and version, the Principles version, the profile, the Notes version, and the normalisations applied (also recorded in the transcription's machine-readable metadata, the sidecar).

notes.title: Purpose of the report
notes.statement: The report is for readers who need to know how the score differs from its source. It should be possible to read the score without the report, and to recover what the source prints from the two together.

notes.title: Observations
notes.statement: If you notice something that looks like a source error, a divergence between parts or repeated passages, or a question an editor would want to ask, record it as an observation in a separate section of the report, not in the score. Say where it is, what the source prints, and why it caught your eye. Observations are not decisions. An observation about a clear error (`correct.error-test`) names the one minimal change.

notes.title: Do not resolve
notes.statement: Do not choose between readings, supply missing material or "improve" the score. A correction is made only for a clear error (`correct.error-test`), and only where the profile allows it.

notes.title: Downstream editions
notes.statement: Anyone preparing an edition (harmonising recurring motives or articulation across parts, adding suggested accidentals, choosing between sources, dropping the source's own brackets) should start from a pinned VoR version, work in their own project, and report every change there. Use an established scheme to record the interventions, such as the editorial markup in MEI or TEI. The previous guide's consistency edits, 'obvious' corrections and editorial accidentals belong at this layer.

notes.title: Collating sources
notes.statement: A collation records where transcriptions of the same work differ, without choosing between them. It is a derived view and never part of a transcription. Editions may use it as a starting point.
